messages:
claire (PM): ACME asked for a pilot-level promise: 'burst window' objective of 99.95% success for requests served from their reserved pool in 15m windows. They also want p90/p95 queue-depth autoscale hooks, a prewarm webhook, and an acceptance checklist. Can we scope a safe pilot commitment by EOW? cc @anne @raj @olivia

anne (Eng): Quick clarifying q: 'success' = low error rate (5xx) or bounded latency for admitted requests? Different engineering work.

raj (Infra): Email seemed focused on errors/timeouts during spikes. We can expose a webhook + prewarm API; if config is operator-facing YAML only, rough estimate 2 sprints. UI = more time.

olivia (SRE): 99.95% in 15m windows is tight. We should only treat it as a pilot target and require automatic fallback to hosted models + circuit breaker before committing. Also need a rollback/runbook.

sam (Support): ACME wants per-request audit logs and tenant traces. We can provide dashboards; need to confirm retention and PII handling with them.

claire (PM): Proposed pilot MVP to present: operator-configurable autoscale triggers + webhook prewarm (soft prewarm), canary cutover path with automatic fallback to hosted model variant, QA acceptance checklist and a cutover runbook. Any objections or reductions?

anne (Eng): Canary + fallback reduces blast radius. If triggers are operator-config only (no product UI) we can accelerate. Rough dev estimate: ~6 dev-weeks (2w design + 4w implement + tests).

raj (Infra): Prototype config snippet to put in ticket:
```
autoscale:
  trigger:
    metric: queue_depth_p95
    threshold: 120
    window: 60s
  action:
    prewarm: 2-gpus
    timeout: 300s
```
We can wire this to prewarm/autoscaler hooks.

olivia (SRE): QA checklist highlights: load test at 2x expected burst, chaos test (region/GPU failure) verify fallback, canary ramp and rollback thresholds, alerts for queue depth/tail-latency/error-rate.

claire (PM): Draft acceptance items (label as pilot objective, not contractual): pilot target (15m->99.95% success), example autoscale YAML, canary plan & rollback thresholds, telemetry access and retention, KMS/HSM check, cutover runbook.

marco (Legal): Do not promise SLA in external materials or contract without amendment. Call it a 'pilot target'; Legal will draft any amendment if requested.

claire (PM): Agreed. We'll present as pilot target. Next steps: @anne add estimates to ticket by EOD tomorrow, @raj prototype webhook + config mock by Thu, @olivia baseline tests by Wed, @sam confirm logging/retention with ACME. Reconvene Fri 11am unless blockers.

deploy-bot: ticket PIOT-342 created by @claire: "ACME reserved-pool burst pilot - autoscale hooks + QA"

anne (Eng): Adding estimates now.

olivia (SRE): Spinning up test harness skeleton and benchmark plan; will share Wed.

sam (Support): Confirming logging details with ACME and scheduling cutover coverage.

claire (PM): Thanks all, closing loop.
